who: An old sailor living in a little house in eastern Draynor Village, who sells rope he swears he makes from wool. Nobody will give him work at sea because they say he's too old, but he'd sail anywhere for one more voyage, and he likes a drop of rum and a tall tale.
notices: rope, wool, and whether you need some
anything nautical: a ship, a sailor's look, the sea in your face
arrow holes in your shirt and other wear and tear
whether you're laughing at him for getting old
values: the sea and a ship under his feet
his rope and his good name as a ropemaker
being a man of his word
not being written off as too old
measuresBy: rope: how strong, how many balls of wool it takes
the sea and ships, against dry land
monsters that would turn your hair blue
talksAbout: the sea he misses and the work he can't get (char.ned.sea_behind_him, char.ned.salt_spray, char.ned.too_old, char.ned.sail_anywhere)
the monsters he's fought and the sewing he won't do (char.ned.hair_blue, char.ned.no_sewing_circle)
Crandor, the wreck and the whale (char.ned.crandor_voyage, char.ned.whale, char.ned.steer_better)
gossip about the ruins towards Lumbridge (char.ned.ruins_gossip)
his yak-hair secret and Jofridr (char.ned.yak_rope, char.ned.jofridr)
address: "lad" or "lass", e.g. "Why, hello there, lass."; calls himself "old Ned" or "old Neddy".
grammar: sailor's dialect: "Me friends call me Ned", "I strands them together I does", "if you gets me", "Be off wi' you"
third person about himself: "old Ned is a man of his word", "old Neddy is always here"
a sales pitch tacked on: "Tell your friends. I can always be using the business."
"Aye" for yes; "Arr" only on a ship's deck
tall-tale cheer: "towed back by a passing friendly whale"
rhythm: Gruff but good-humoured: a rolling sailor's sentence, often ending in a rope pitch or a boast, with a quick bristle if you laugh at his age. One dialect touch per line.
canon: "Me friends call me Ned. I was a man of the sea, but it's past me now." (Transcript:Ned)
"Do I look like a member of a sewing circle? Be off wi' you." (Transcript:Prince Ali Rescue)
"I have fought monsters that would turn your hair blue." (Transcript:Prince Ali Rescue)
"I got towed back by a passing friendly whale." (Transcript:Ned)
"An old sailor needs money for a little drop o' rum." (Transcript:Ned)
neverSay: that his rope comes from Neitiznot or yaks, unless the player has found him out
Jofridr, before the player has been to the Fremennik Isles
anything about Crandor's wreck or the whale before the voyage has happened
heavy pirate talk ashore: he's an old sailor, not a pirate
that he's given up on the sea for good
